### Delivered concrete reader and boundaries

`agent.TranscriptSelection` has a zero/current variant and an owned exact
`big.Int` value. `SelectTranscriptEpoch` supports concrete backend epoch values;
`SelectTranscriptEpochNumber` copies arbitrary exact query integers. No generic
payload or raw JSON is retained in service/domain state. Concrete
`TranscriptSnapshot` names session/epoch/highest-epoch/messages, and
`TranscriptEpochNotFound` names the requested decimal identity and current epoch.

`ManagedSession.ReadTranscript(ctx, selection)` reads the configured backend,
validates supported message roles/closed content and returns detached copies.
It briefly snapshots persistence configuration, releases that mutex before
backend I/O, passes cancellation into metadata/message reads and checks it before
publication and during copying. Reads do not flush live history, acquire a lease,
start a model turn, repair tool calls, mutate writer error state or install human
permissions. A foreign-held pending-restoration handle can read its unrepaired
stored history without changing the holder or claim count. Library callers own
authorization; the HTTP adapter performs owner admission before backend access.

The HTTP adapter uses concrete query-issue variants and a two-element location,
matching the captured 422 shapes. Opaque 503 handles backend read errors/panics
before writing any transcript body; unlike source uncaught backend faults, this
is an explicit Go addition. There is no live/raw fallback. Metadata selection
and message loading are separate backend reads, matching the source; no database
snapshot transaction is claimed. An epoch returns its full stored message array,
not a newly introduced pagination/truncation policy.

The synchronized test backing now reports epoch zero for no stored messages,
including empty append bookkeeping. The former empty-restore test expected a
phantom stored epoch 1; it now compares the actual source's zero while runtime
restoration still starts its next write at at least one. Python runtime/package
code is unchanged. Native Go SQL, backend launcher selection, unsupported
state/provider variants, optional feature groups and release audit remain open.

## Implementation checkpoint — 2026-10-06 typed decisions and Jev operator library

Baseline `6f4a4b0`; P0/P1 remain complete, G0–G7 remain open. The previously
unported decision contracts and Jev backend now have a native typed operator
library. This is the first prerequisite of the explicit decision migration
sequence above; it does not substitute for the required gate/LLM/configuration,
masking/event/limiter and large-result replay integration.

### Actual source contract and native implementation

- `go/decisions` adds closed ValueKind (null/string/number/boolean/array/object),
  Question/Answer variants, Request/Result/TokenUsage and Provider. State and
  descriptions carry only the closed Value union; domain/service structs retain
  no any, interface{}, map[string]any or json.RawMessage. Open decoder tokens
  are lowered at the boundary. Test fixtures alone use raw JSON to express
  malformed inputs. Constructor/accessor copies detach nested state, rubric,
  probability, answer and usage containers.
- Source request limits are retained: 1..32 questions, choice 1..255 criteria,
  score 2..10 levels, nonempty instructions, 128 KiB compact UTF-8 JSON and
  nesting depth 32. Empty state remains valid. Result IDs/types must match;
  distributions cover the complete requested set and sum to one within 1e-5;
  choice names a maximum, and score/legend match the weighted ordered rubric.
  Noul is a finite yes probability without invented confidence. Whole usage
  can be unavailable for custom adapters; Jev requires both token counts.
- Integer versus float spelling survives wire decoding, including probabilities,
  score and confidence, without retaining raw JSON. Source float exponent/decimal
  projection and signed zero are retained in closed Values. Exact integer/binary
  float legend equality avoids rounding different large integers together and
  preserves Python's nested numeric/boolean description equality.
- Jev defaults come from the current Python source: fixed systemone endpoint,
  model alias jev-latest, total 20 s timeout and two retries. Explicit bounds are
  (0,120] s and 0..3 retries. Construction performs no network request. Only
  429/529 retry; Retry-After clamps at two seconds, with bounded invalid-header
  fallback. One context deadline covers attempts, reads and sleeps. Bodies close
  before retry and on terminal paths; reads stop after 512 KiB plus one sentinel
  byte. Redirects are disabled on private clients, actual served provenance is
  retained and transport/raw-response feedback is sanitized.
- Owned clients use a fresh transport without environment proxies and close idle
  connections after each evaluation. Injected clients are shallow-copied only to
  install redirect policy; transports remain caller-owned. Provider evaluation
  revalidates/snapshots its request and supports concurrent independent calls.
  The library does not implicitly mask, collect context or grant execution
  authority: the explicit operator caller owns those choices. Runtime gate and
  LLM composition remain pending; default tools, HTTP operations and launcher
  decision refusal are unchanged.

## Implementation checkpoint — 2026-10-06 anchored publication file boundary

The source publisher requires descriptor-anchored component traversal and a
no-replace hard link. Go 1.23 Darwin's public syscall package lacks the required
at helpers, so native durable confines typed syscall wrappers/pointers to one
boundary and platform constants to separate files. Apple XNU revision
f6217f891ac0bb64f3d375211650a4c1ff8ca1ea, bsd/kern/syscalls.master, confirms
463/471/472; the installed Go 1.23.3 Darwin syscall assembly confirms the kernel
entry convention. Linux uses architecture-specific Go constants. No dependency,
cgo, path-based replacement or process-wide chdir is introduced.

CreateText uses component-wise O_DIRECTORY/O_NOFOLLOW/CLOEXEC, exact private
scratch mode, file fsync and same-descriptor linkat. Typed device/inode identity
is prepared before linking. Link success commits; post-link cleanup, directory
fsync and close cannot turn success into error. ReadBytesNoFollow verifies regular
files and reads one extra byte to detect overflow. Native NONBLOCK avoids hostile
FIFO hangs. Cancellation is checked before the commit point. Anchoring survives
parent relocation, which is not a proof of global filesystem tenancy/fencing.

file/directory/links, parent link and link/.. refusal, exact/oversized/empty reads,
file bytes, private mode, identity and scratch cleanup. Native tests add 20

replaced by a symlink after opening, and FIFO refusal.

## Native SQLite compaction restart proof — 2026-10-10

`go/sqlitestate/compaction_restart_test.go` composes the real manager, compress
and read_file tool batch, default archive/summary path and native SQLite backend.
Three cases cover a successful summary, provider failure and cancellation.
The archive must contain the complete paired three-message tool batch, including
the later read_file result. Successful compaction stores a summary in epoch 2
while retaining the exact paired epoch 1; the summary receipt is persisted with
its Source-compatible pre-rewrite epoch and archive path. Failure/cancellation
writes the archive but preserves the paired canonical epoch 1 without a summary
receipt. Tests close and reopen the database before explicit manager restoration.
They check owner/identity/run count, exact current and historical messages,
unchanged persisted event prefix, resumed provider request prefix, healthy lease
state, archive bytes and retained superseded epoch after the resumed turn.

This proves the composed small-history compaction/restart path. It does not
extend the proof to arbitrary large archival profiles or claim all G5/G7 work
complete. Default diagnostics selection and full migration acceptance remain open.

interactive map are unchanged. Runtime code, Python sources and contracts are
unchanged in this iteration.

## Native reload build and artifact ownership — 2026-10-10

`reload.NewBuilder` captures explicit trusted module/package/toolchain configuration
and a detached environment. One local package is selected; option-shaped, wildcard
and parent-escaping targets are refused. Build uses the existing Go executable,
`-mod=readonly`, the current host OS/architecture and `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` to prevent
implicit toolchain downloads. This native compilation stage is the Go development
adaptation; Python StatReload restarts an interpreter and has no corresponding
native build artifact. No new dependency is added.

Each attempt allocates a private 0700 temporary output directory and streams
compiler diagnostics to its caller. Errors/cancellation clean the directory before
returning. Successful output must be a regular Go executable, checked with standard
library buildinfo, with owner-only executable mode and a retained SHA-256.
Artifact.Executable rechecks regular-file shape, execute permission and bytes;
Artifact.Close releases only its own temporary directory and is idempotent.
The consumer must stop/join its running child before closing its artifact.
Builder diagnostics are opaque to fmt so retained environment credentials are not
exposed by incidental formatting. Compiler diagnostics remain caller-owned.

The build command owns a distinct process session/group on macOS/Linux. Caller
cancellation kills it; command completion also removes lingering helpers. A
bounded WaitDelay handles inherited diagnostic pipes. Other platforms retain the
existing direct-process cancellation fallback; no descendant-group guarantee is
claimed there. Actual native tests compile syntax-invalid source, prove failed
output cleanup, repair and run two changed binaries, reject library archives,
refuse modified/closed artifacts and verify detached private configuration.
An explicit test toolchain spawns a real helper holding pipes; cancellation joins
the command, removes output and leaves no running helper on macOS/Linux.

This is an explicit SDK component. It does not yet own a server child or listener;
CLI reload remains refused until the supervisor and HTTP process proof are wired.
README review/boundary and architecture metadata identify the separate owners.
Python sources, contract exports and existing guard/scanner anchors are unchanged.

## Native reload supervisor and retained listener — 2026-10-10

`reload.NewSupervisor` captures typed Builder/Watcher collaborators, child working
directory, arguments and environment. On macOS/Linux its single-use Run owns an
admitted TCP listener. The parent retains that socket through replacement, build
failure and child exit. The public child protocol duplicates inherited descriptor
3 into a TCP listener; actual-address authentication remains the caller's duty.
This is an explicit SDK; config still refuses MINILOOP_RELOAD. CLI selection and
actual miniloop HTTP proof remain required. No dependency is introduced.

An edit stops/joins the old child before compiling/replacing it. SIGTERM gets a
finite configurable grace (default 10 seconds), followed by forced process-group
termination. Wait joins children and cleans their private artifacts before the
parent closes its listener. Build/start errors and unexpected child exits emit
typed events and keep observing for a correction, without a respawn loop.
Callback panics trigger owned cleanup and an error; callbacks/writers must return
promptly. Cancellation after a successful build also closes the returned artifact.
Native builds explicitly select executable mode. Priming before each build keeps
edits during compilation visible. These bounded/native details are documented Go
adaptations; Source StatReload restarts an interpreter and joins without this
native build stage. Other platforms refuse supervisor admission before ownership.

Actual HTTP child tests import the public inherited-listener helper, replace
three generations at one address, join old children, retain the socket through
syntax failure, recover after repair, and release socket/artifacts on shutdown.
Additional real children ignore SIGTERM to prove forced cleanup; callback-panic
cleanup is verified. Detached environment and single-use rejection are checked.

edge/default; boundary/review baseline and aggregate interactive card updated.

## 2026-10-10 Typed dynamic credentials and process-local token cache

Baseline `65ac890` plus this slice adds immutable validated AccessToken and
CredentialProvider.FetchToken(context, force) as an explicit provider injection
seam. Named CredentialError kinds retain classification/status without raw
exchange bodies or callback messages. Construction/description perform no fetch.
Each Client owns one synchronized cache; direct and streaming views share it.
No token provider is installed by default, and provider/file lifetime remains
caller-owned. This is the prerequisite for native profile/federation drivers,
not their completed discovery/HTTP exchange implementation.

The cache follows the inspected pinned SDK: >120s/no expiry serves cached;
>30s and <=120s starts advisory refresh while concurrent callers retain cached tokens;
<=30s/missing cache joins one refresh. Recoverable typed credential errors permit
advisory fallback with five-second backoff; invalid/callback errors propagate.
Token-endpoint exchange 401 retries once with force=true. Explicit invalidation
forces a subsequent fetch without cancelling/fencing an in-flight provider.
Model HTTP 401 does not invalidate credentials or replay a request.

Context-owned waits can cancel independently; callbacks must honor context.
Panic/error paths always release mandatory waiters. Static effective API-key/
Authorization headers bypass dynamic callbacks. Dynamic tokens add the OAuth
API beta using whole-flag deduplication. Direct/SSE attempts retain a private
request-local token solely for diagnostic redaction; overlapping requests keep
their own token after a shared-cache rotation. Callback diagnostics are generic
credential failures; exchange failures keep WorkloadIdentityError/status while
ordinary typed credential failures use AnthropicError. No raw callback message
is projected into model-facing errors.

Tests cover exact 121/120/30-second boundaries, advisory backoff, forced exchange
retry, joined/cancelled waits, panic recovery, static bypass, direct/stream model
401 caching/no replay, beta normalization and concurrent old/new-token response
redaction. Provider package race passes. This uses the prior SDK source/26
discovery recipes as the reference; native file-profile/refresh/federation replay
of that whole fixture remains open. README canonical Mermaid/boundary, EXTENDING

## 2026-10-10 explicit native federation token exchange

Code/test baseline: `a43b1da` plus this implementation. Installed Source SDK
Anthropic 0.107.1 WorkloadIdentityCredentials __call__/__init__/bind_base_url,
IdentityTokenFile and constants define exchange semantics. Six existing pinned
Source recipes compare native construction/request/error/cache behavior:
federation-environment, file-before-literal, refuses-http, exchange-failure,
model-401 and file-rotation. These tests supply explicit captured identity sources;
they do not prove the still-pending Launcher environment/profile discovery chain.

`provider.NewFederation` implements CredentialProvider with named rule,
organization and optional service-account/workspace fields. Optional values are
copied, preserving absent versus empty. Scope is copied informational metadata,
never sent. One deployment URL owns direct exchange/model selection. Each fetch
re-invokes IdentityTokenProvider, including forced retries. Literal sources capture
the string and validate on fetch; IdentityTokenFile reopens a projected token,
follows rotated symlinks and retains Python strip whitespace semantics. Source
assertion/response caps are 16 KiB/1 MiB; default exchange timeout is 30 seconds.
The closed JWT assertion carries no interpreted claims or local authority.

The jwt-bearer request sends OAuth and federation beta flags; model auth sends
OAuth beta only. Optional/None bearer token_type and case-insensitive Bearer are
accepted; expires_in is required and uses PythonInteger conversion. Checked
civil-time expiry retains the documented 0001–9999 native bound. Client's existing
cache owns reuse/advisory/mandatory windows and one forced token-endpoint 401
retry. Model 401 does not invalidate/replay. The driver itself caches/writes
nothing. Response statuses below 400 can supply a valid token as in Source.

Native adaptations retain strict UTF-8/string/header ingress, an 8 MiB raw-file
cap before strip, parsed exact-loopback HTTP admission, refused redirects on a

## Continuous Darwin owner lifetime — 2026-10-11

Baseline: `0027a97` plus this implementation. Pinned notify 8 runs a fresh
owner thread in CFRunLoopRun; the prior Go implementation re-entered 50ms slices
and returned its owner OS thread to the Go pool. Darwin now runs continuously
on a locked thread that retires at goroutine exit. An opaque C MiniLoopEvents
owns the stream, loop and version-zero stop source. Close signals that source
and wakes the loop; its callback stops on the owner thread, retaining an early
signal before loop entry. The signalling call is joined before C objects are
released. Unexpected loop return fails the reader, with caller Close still owed.

The stop protocol follows Apple's [custom input-source signalling guidance](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/documentation/Cocoa/Conceptual/Multithreading/RunLoopManagement/RunLoopManagement.html).
Callback admission, roots, batch/context deadlines and all Source recipe fixtures
are unchanged. No global device purge or dependencies added. This is Source
lifecycle alignment, not a claim to resolve the historical timeout cause.

## Event-boundary interruption verification — 2026-10-11

Test implementation commit: `a7f873e`; baseline `d060ac2`.
The Python interrupted-turn helper previously slept 120ms before cancellation,
which did not establish that a stream had entered or shown a partial response.
It now wraps the actual session event capture, waits for assistant_delta, and
holds the captured event boundary until cancellation. Partial-answer and thinking
claims wait for their specific text. A ten-second readiness failure bound prevents
an absent event hanging the test; it is not a widened production/observer deadline.
